doc.title: Buddy Burns and Frank Pasley Interview, 1968-09-23

title: Drive 'Em Down and Son Miller
summary: Burns explains that Son Miller played the blues Drive 'Em Down and was older than he.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Where the blues came from: Handy, Bolden and early blues

blocks.x: No, not, drive him down, this piano player.

Oh, drive him down. Well, then that's what we call Son Miller, drive him down, because he played some dirty blues and then also his brother, Butzi. Butzi? Yeah, Butzi Miller. Butzi Miller. Butzi Miller.
Is Son Miller still in New Orleans?
Yeah. He, what does he look at? I don't know if he did, or what, tall, slim, tall, brown skin, tall, tall, about six foot four.
He's not related to Sing Miller?
And you call him drive him down?

That's the name of the blues. If we call him drive him down on the count, that's what he used to play. Oh, yeah, I see. Drive him down. And was he older than you? Oh, yeah. How many? He must be about six, seven years, something like that.
